newsitem.title: JORDAN: PRESS DIGEST - Jordan - March 1. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Jordan - March 1. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliamentary sources expect the prime minister to go ahead with cabinet reshuffle after the end of parliamentary session on March 19. Elections as scheduled later in the year.
- King Hussein says Israel's settlement building in Jerusalem threatens the Middle East peace process.
- Eight political parties expect to merge to form National Constitutional Party.
- Jordan celebrates 41 years (corrects from 40 years) since removal of British general "Glubb Pasha" as head of Arab Legion, starting the "Arabisation" of Jordan's army.
- Engineers Union, continuing their pay dispute with Ministry of Labour, to protest in front of prime minister's office today.
- Interior minister says government has dealt with administrative corruption.
- Arab Banking Corporation official says some Jordanian banks have decided to raise interest rates this year on loans to around 14-16 percent.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for dialogue that strengthens responsible citizenship and national unity.
- No more censorship of foreign papers, magazines.
- King Hussein: Netanyahu should not think informing in advance will make his plans acceptable.
